rounds.text: The market is fundamentally mispricing Rishabh Digha Steel & Allied Products Ltd by hyper-focusing on backward-looking metrics while ignoring an explosive acceleration in recent revenue. While 10-year compounded sales growth sits at a stagnant -5% [E14], looking at longer-term figures obscures a massive structural turnaround: 5-year compounded sales growth reaches 20% [E15] and 3-year compounded sales growth explodes to an astonishing 361% [E16]. This remarkable top-line scaling is further confirmed by recent quarter-over-quarter sales momentum [E61]. Furthermore, the valuation disconnect is glaring when assessing asset backing rather than distorted earnings multiples. The company trades at a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.04x on a book value of ₹ 33.6 per share [E2], representing a deep discount compared to the broader sector benchmark price-to-book ratio of 2.58x [E7]. This conservative valuation is underscored by a market capitalization of just ₹ 19.2 Cr [E3] and a position sitting at only 42% of its 52-week range [E5]. Adding to this compelling fundamental picture, recent data shows profit growth exceeding 1-year price growth by 128%, signaling that the company is starting to outperform market expectations [E55] while operating against a robust sector median sales growth of 18.7% [E70]. Conceded: trailing twelve months sales growth is down -7% [E17], sales fell -43% year-over-year [E64], and earnings growth is decelerating [E65].
